findings.issue_text: Default blank embed_category causes migration to raise before uncategorized fallback runs
Legacy host values are not normalized during migration, so scheme-prefixed hosts no longer match URI host authorization
Validation permits hosts with ports, but lookup discards ports so saved hosts never match embed requests
Duplicate hosts with different categories make category selection nondeterministic because the query uses unordered first
Hydration deletes *_ids when referenced records are absent, silently losing relationship data in partial REST responses
New hosts assigned the uncategorized category display with no category until reload because the success handler uses the unchanged null categoryId
Updating a deleted or nonexistent host passes nil to save_host and returns 500 instead of 404

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Validation permits hosts with ports, but lookup discards ports so saved hosts never match embed requests

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the EmbeddableHost model has a validation regex that allows ports: `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\/i`. However, the before_validation strips the protocol and path but NOT the port: `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` and `self.host.sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`. So a host like 'example.com:8080' could be saved. In the `record_for_host` method, it does `uri = URI(host)` then `host = uri.host`. When you call `URI('http://example.com:8080').host`, it returns just 'example.com' without the port. So if someone saves 'example.com:8080' as an embeddable host, and then a request comes from 'http://example.com:8080/page', the lookup would search for 'example.com' (without port) but the database has 'example.com:8080', so it wouldn't match. This is a real bug where hosts with ports can be saved but will never match incoming requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate hosts with different categories make category selection nondeterministic because the query uses unordered first

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the EmbeddableHost.record_for_host method, it queries with `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` without any ordering. If there are multiple embeddable hosts with the same hostname but different categories, the result would depend on database ordering which is nondeterministic. However, examining the model validation and the host field, the validation `validates_format_of :host` doesn't prevent duplicate hosts. The `before_validation` strips protocol and path, so 'http://example.com' and 'https://example.com' would both become 'example.com'. Without a uniqueness constraint on host, duplicates are possible, and `first` without ordering would return an arbitrary record. This is a real correctness issue - the category selection for embedded topics could be unpredictable if duplicate hosts exist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hydration deletes *_ids when referenced records are absent, silently losing relationship data in partial REST responses

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the _hydrateEmbedded function in store.js.es6, when handling plural IDs (m[2] is truthy for '_ids'), the code maps over the IDs and calls _lookupSubType for each. If _lookupSubType returns undefined/null for any ID, those values end up in the hydrated array. The code then does `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || [];` and `delete obj[k];`. The issue is that `delete obj[k]` happens unconditionally for plural IDs, even when some lookups fail. However, the hydrated array still contains the results (even if some are undefined). For singular IDs, the delete only happens `if (hydrated)`. This is a real behavioral difference - for plural IDs, the original *_ids array is always deleted regardless of whether hydration succeeded, while for singular IDs, the original *_id is preserved if hydration fails. This could cause data loss in partial REST responses where referenced records aren't included.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New hosts assigned the uncategorized category display with no category until reload because the success handler uses the unchanged null categoryId

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the save action in embeddable-host.js.es6, when saving a new host: `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId');` where categoryId starts as null. In the controller's save_host method, if category_id is blank, it defaults to uncategorized: `host.category_id = SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id if host.category_id.blank?`. However, in the success handler: `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')));` - this uses the original null categoryId, not the server-assigned uncategorized_category_id. So the category will be set to null/undefined until the page is reloaded, even though the server correctly saved the uncategorized category. This is a real UI bug.
